skill_friction: Design rule 'when the change makes existing descriptions or instructions false, updating them is part of the inventory' forced an ApexClass Update for a description-only string (itemsJson 'Only name is required per item'); in an org with no test classes this adds deployment coverage risk for a cosmetic change. The skill does not say whether description drift in an Apex @InvocableVariable warrants an Apex deploy versus a proposal.

GenAiFunction input schema (where agent-facing input descriptions are copied) cannot be read with the allowed commands, so the GenAiFunction row can only be Conditional; the skill has no guidance for this specific unreadable-schema case.

The 'two wrong AskCoworker claims' counter is ambiguous about what counts: D1/D2's 'validation rules are not SOQL-queryable' (same claim twice) and I's over-broad Apex guard proposal were counted as two; T's wrong claims (GenAiFunction may not exist, existing test class) arrived after the threshold.

No guidance on an existing non-atomic writer (insert parent then children, catch without Savepoint) whose partial-commit behavior becomes more frequent because of the new rule; treated as a proposal per 'defect the requirement does not depend on'.
run.json seq numbers are integers, but an extra org query inserted between steps needed a fractional seq (13.5).
